question: Does actor objective or timeliness of value readout explain the DeepSea gap to native CQL?
primary: Normalized trapezoidal mean expected return over 0..2048 updates; full continuation 8192.
selection: Best across-development-seed early mean among the 24 PDR actor/coefficient configurations, separately per N. Ties by condition id. Freeze winner before heldout runs; no heldout retuning.
control: Native discrete SAC-CQL with previously selected per-size conservatism/entropy, unchanged actor/critic learning rates, replay schedules, full support, initial model/optimizer/RNG state and evaluation.
crossed_critic: Every branch uses identical CQL critic loss/update rule and twin-head initialization. Trajectories can then diverge through current-policy targets.
pdr: Full exact soft-policy differential at fixed CQL entropy; same current-policy soft evaluation operator as CQL target. Fixed exact soft Qold from initial policy. Actor value alpha*Qold + beta*D; centers to alpha*Aref + beta*DeltaA.
semantics: PDR-SAC is an extension to a different actor backbone, explicitly labelled. It is not a renamed AWAC checkpoint or a claim that critic objectives are unchanged from historical OURS.
inference: Original seeds are development data; new paired 20-seed validation uses only eligible predeclared starts with failures retained. No seed selection by OURS performance.
checkpoints: Complete initial/final models, targets, optimizers and RNG; exact input hashes and schedules.
